subject: every scoring-relevant rule of the 2025 MSCA Doctoral Networks evaluation, read against the 2026 profile
purpose: The runbook proposes preparing a historical profile as a copy of the 2026 one, leaving a rule unchanged where no source states a difference. That is a defaulting policy, not evidence that the rule applied in 2025. This matrix replaces it: each rule is sourced to a 2025 document, or recorded as defaulted with the rule its defaulting affects, or recorded as an unresolved limitation. No verdict means that no difference was found.
declared_status_note: Inferred, not Confirmed. Every sourced row rests on a pinned document whose bytes nothing from an issuing body vouches for, and harness.authority_matrix.check refuses a Confirmed row on such a source.
supersedes: the equivalence matrix authored on 2026-10-12, `docs/tier4_orchestration_state/msca_dn/authority/equivalence_matrix_2025_2026-10-12.json` (sha256 115949d3fe4858340128a6ce1fc3afe83f28a085347714752ccf1ca9d9453bcd). That matrix carried six defaulted rows and two unresolved, every one of them resting on a 2025 document this repository did not hold. Three of those documents have since been obtained, so the six defaultings are re-derived here against the sources themselves and one new row records a difference they revealed. The superseded matrix stays in the tree unedited: a correction to a matrix is a successor matrix, and what was believed on 2026-10-12 is part of the evidence. The specification's decision 3, which pinned one 2026 profile because the 2025 sources were absent, stands as written.
uncertainties: No row is defaulted. Two are unresolved, and each names what is missing: the binding of this submission to a call, and the evaluation form version the 2025 evaluators were given.

Twenty-five rows are Inferred and none is Confirmed. Every 2025 document here is hashed in this tree and none carries a hash published by its issuing body, so no row may be Confirmed on byte integrity. Three documents are corroborated by a second independent copy, which raises what is known about their origin and not about what governed the call.

Two 2025 authorities state different score resolutions. The work programme says one decimal place, the evaluation form says half marks. TH-05 shows which was applied to this submission, from a recorded score no half-mark rule could award. It does not resolve the conflict in general, and a statement about any other 2025 proposal must carry it.

Every row citing the 2025 evaluation form inherits EI-02's bracket. Three captures of one archive are one witness observed three times, and a version served between two captures and never captured would leave no trace.

The 2025 application form has no recorded origin, and nothing establishes it was the version in force. The five rows citing it are Inferred for that reason, and retrieving a corroborating copy of it is not attempted here.

A sourced row claims what its citations measure and no more. SM-01 compares the aspect anchors in both directions; AM-01 claims an inclusion only, so a 2025 cross-reference the 2026 mapping has no row for would not have been seen.

Whether an area's rows are all of its scoring-relevant rules is this author's judgement. The check reads what each row cites and refuses an unsourced relation; it cannot report a rule nobody wrote a row for.

The rows sourced to the 2025 evaluation's own record settle what was applied to this submission. None of them settles a rule of the 2025 call, and the check refuses a call-wide claim resting only on them.

EI-01, the six score-level descriptions, was the largest unsourced input to a numerical comparison. All six sentences are now located in the 2025 form, word for word, so the comparison no longer rests on a 2026 document alone.

This matrix quotes the 2025 evaluation's recorded figures. It lives beside the ESR record, outside the dev-graph root, and is not snapshotted; the blind lane's isolation rests on that exclusion and on the assessor running with no tools from outside the repository, exactly as it does for the ESR record itself.
isolation_note: Written under docs/tier4_orchestration_state/msca_dn/, outside the dev-graph root at workspaces/msca_dn/. No snapshot reads it, so it cannot reach an evidence pack, which is the position the ESR record already holds (specification decision 12).
authority_note: This matrix confers no authority and closes no gate. It records what the sources state. A row marked defaulted is a declaration that a rule is unsourced, not a finding that it is wrong, and a row marked equivalent is a statement about the documents cited rather than about every rule of the call.

rows.rule: Which call the 2025 submission was evaluated under. Every other row's 2025 side is addressed to this call.
rows.status_basis: Two records declare the identifier Assumed and give the same reason. The value is the operator's declaration, and this module refuses to render if either record stops declaring it Assumed. The work programme now evidences that a call with that identifier existed, with the dates it cites. It does not evidence that this submission was made to it, which is what the row is about, so the status stays Assumed.
rows.limitation: The call itself is now pinned. The work programme part states its identifier, its opening date and its deadline, so the call this submission is declared against exists and its conditions are held. What is still missing is the binding: the Evaluation Summary Report names no proposal number, and nothing in this repository shows this submission was entered into that call. Two records declare the binding, and a declaration is not evidence of it.
rows.consequence: The historical profile carries the operator's declared call identifier with declared_status Assumed, never Confirmed, and the matrix is cited as the reason.
